subject: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs. VendorX (PulseHealth)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@pulsehealth.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs. VendorX (PulseHealth)

Hi Samir / Alicia,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the candid discussion. Quick recap from our call so everyone has the same view and next steps for the bake-off. Please flag anything I missed.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Primary pain: inconsistent inference latency causing timeouts in the patient support chat flow (95th percentile ~2.5s) and high per-token costs on current provider.
- Data & compliance: logs must be kept for 12 months, audit trail required for PHI access, and key management via customer KMS is a hard requirement.
- Success metrics: reduce 95th latency to <=1.2s for typical 256-token prompts, cut per-token cost by ~30%, and pass SOC 2 evidence review.

Decision criteria (what PulseHealth cares about)
1) Latency guarantees & SLOs (regionally routed)
2) Cost / unit economics at expected QPS
3) Security/compliance (KMS, VPC, audit logs)
4) Model quality on the triage/routing prompts
5) Operational support and runbook readiness for production cutover

Competitive landscape
- VendorX (Tom) will run a parallel test focusing on their newer quantized runtime; they called out lower-list price but higher variance in tail latency.
- Redwood will focus on predictable latency via our Dedicated routing and KV prefix caching, plus a targeted test exercising your patient-support prompts.

Open questions from PulseHealth
- Can Redwood run within their VPC or do we need a private deployment?
- What specific audit artifacts do we provide for SOC 2?
- How do rollouts and canarying work if we need to flip traffic gradually?

Proposed bake-off plan (next 2 weeks)
- PulseHealth to share the requirements sheet with test prompts and expected QPS (Samir/Alicia) — attach to this thread (thanks for sending).
- Redwood to deliver an MVP test plan for the bake-off and a test harness to run A/B comparisons against VendorX (we'll share by end of day Tue).
- Kickoff technical test on Wed (Jul 21) — 2 hours: load generator, sample prompts, and collection of latency/cost traces.
- Redwood to provide SOC 2 artifact list and a short runbook for canary cutover.

Attachments: pulse_requirements.xlsx (you mentioned this on the call)

Next steps / action owners
- Samir: share requirements sheet & confirm timeline for internal decision (expected by Aug 6).
- Alicia: confirm who on engineering will join the Wed test.
- Marissa: deliver bake-off test plan + share a short list of required artifacts by Tue EOD.
- Aditya / Rishi: stand by to join the test and help on performance tuning.

Thanks — I'll follow up with the test plan tomorrow.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference | +1 415-555-0147

Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs. VendorX (PulseHealth)

Marissa — thanks for the thorough note. This lines up with our internal view. A few clarifications:

- I've attached the requirements workbook (pulse_requirements.xlsx) — contains test prompts, sample traffic mix, and current monthly token volumes.
- Timeline: Decision committee meets week of Aug 2; technical evaluation must be complete by Jul 28 for scoring.
- SOC 2: security will need encryption-at-rest proof and a list of endpoints that will touch PHI. We can share the SOC 2 questionnaire with either vendor.

A couple of asks for Redwood before the test:
1) Can you confirm whether the Dedicated option can be provisioned in our us-west-2 region?
2) What observable metrics will you provide during the test (we need per-route 95/99 latency, cost per token breakdown, KV hit rates)?

I'll loop in engineering once we lock the Wed slot — Alicia, can you confirm availability?

Thanks,
Samir
Director, Platform Integrations | PulseHealth
samir.rao@pulsehealth.com | +1 206-555-0199

Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs. VendorX (PulseHealth)

Thanks Samir — received the requirements and timeline. Quick answers and the test plan (attached):

1) Region: Yes — Dedicated pools can be provisioned in us-west-2. We'll provision a small test pool reserved for the bake-off to avoid noisy-neighbor issues.
2) Observability: we'll provide per-route 50/95/99 latency, per-token cost, KV cache hit rate, GPU utilization, and a JMX-like trace for any outliers. We'll push a dashboard link after the first run.

Attached is the MVP test plan (redwood_mvp-test-plan.pdf) — high level:
- Warmup: preload KV cache with prefixes from your traffic sample.
- Test workloads: baseline (current provider), Redwood, VendorX (if you want us to coordinate).
- Measurements: latency distributions, token costs, quality checks on a holdout prompt set (accuracy/fluency), and resource utilization.
- Pass criteria: 95th latency <= 1.2s and <= 30% cost improvement vs baseline, and no security artifact gaps.

Internal note for Aditya/Rishi: please review the test plan and confirm the exact fields we will log (I'll set up a short runbook). If VendorX wants to be included in the same harness, Tom — happy to coordinate test jobs; we need your runtime image and an endpoint by Tue morning.

Proposed kickoff: Wed Jul 21 at 10:00am PT — 2-hour window for load runs and initial dashboard review.

Thanks — attaching the plan now.

Best,
Marissa
